picks.what: Bird’s-eye view, engraving in Merian’s Topographia Prussiae et Pomerelliae
picks.why: walled old and new towns drawn building by building inside the bastions, with the Vistula bridge; cleanest high-resolution copy (BnF Gallica)

picks.file: Anonymous View of Toruń from south (detail) 02.jpg
picks.what: The riverfront and the Vistula bridge, painting, detail (District Museum, Toruń)
picks.why: color view from across the river: city wall, the long bridge and the great square tower of St. John’s; trimmed the dark foreground bank
the classic riverfront with St. John’s and the town walls; the Holy Ghost church tower under construction dates it to 1893–99; trimmed the printed greetings

picks.what: The Old Town and St. John’s Cathedral, photograph from the Old Town Hall tower
picks.why: sharp daylight view over the medieval rooftops to the cathedral and the Vistula; trimmed sky and the tower parapet

gaps: P0, P1: no candidates. P5: no candidates.
notes: #6: the museum dates the painting only to the second half of the 18th century, hence the range label; drop it if that is too loose. It is a detail photographed in the gallery (#5 is another detail of the same painting, western part with ships). #2 is Merian’s bird’s-eye plan (‘Thorunium / Thoren’), first published 1652; #1 and #3 are other copies of the same plate. P4 alternative: #8, the Vistula flood of 1879 (colored wood engraving after H. Penner, an event view, town small in the distance). P6 alternatives: #11 (the riverfront at night, very attractive), #9 (riverfront panorama, too wide at 9:1), #12 (sign in the foreground).
